gandhare-heritage.name: Kargah Buddha
gandhare-heritage.description: About 9.7km away from Gilgit, this carved image is part of an archaeological site which stands 50 feet high.

gandhare-heritage.name: Aror
gandhare-heritage.description: Aror once served as the capital of Sindh. It is mentioned as an important trading center in early Buddhist literature. A massive earthquake that changed the course of the Indus River and ruined the town's mud brick building, thereby setting into play the city's decline.

gandhare-heritage.name: Rock carvings at Thalpan
gandhare-heritage.description: Located at the mid-point between Islamabad and Gilgit-Skardu, the rock carvings at Thalpan are in Chilas Valley, Gilgit

gandhare-heritage.name: Jaulian Buddhist Monastery
gandhare-heritage.description: Dating from the 2nd century CE, Jaulian monastery along with the nearby monastery at Mohra Muradu, form part of the Ruins of Taxila. Consists of a main central stupa, 27 peripheral smaller stupas, 59 small chapels displaying scenes from the life of Buddha.

gandhare-heritage.name: Mankiala Stupa
gandhare-heritage.description: A 2nd-century Buddhist stupa near the village of Tope Mankiala, built to commemorate the spot, where according to the Jataka tales, an incarnation of the Buddha called Prince Sattva sacrificed himself to feed seven hungry tiger cubs.

gandhare-heritage.name: Taxila Museum
gandhare-heritage.description: Taxila Museum is situated in Taxila, its collection mainly focuses on Gandharan art dating from the 1st to the 7th centuries CE.  There are some 4000 objects displayed, including stone, stucco, terracotta, silver, gold, iron and semiprecious stones excavated from the ruins of ancient Taxila.

gandhare-heritage.name: Manthal Buddha Rock
gandhare-heritage.description: Manthal Buddha Rock refers to a giant granite rock on which an image of Buddha has incised that in all probability dates back to the eighth century.

gandhare-heritage.name: Buddhist Stupa Nawabshah
gandhare-heritage.description: A solid cylindrical structure, tapering at the top, constructed with a brick casing about 60 feet in height stands over a square base about 66 feet in each side. Located in the village of Thul Mir Rukan.

sikh-heritage.name: Nankana Sahib
sikh-heritage.description: A small town in Punjab thatâs one of the most sacred locations for Sikhs. The town boasts a beautiful gurdwara with marvelous architecture, which has the power to inspire and amaze.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Panja Sahib
sikh-heritage.description: Gurdwara Panja Sahib Jee is a famous gurdwara located near Islamabad, Hasan Abdal.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Janam Asthan Guru Ram Das Jee
Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee
sikh-heritage.description: Gurdwara Chakki Sahib Jee, at Eminabad is located where a large millstone chakkis was kept.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Sachi Sauda
sikh-heritage.description:
Gudwara sacha sauda is situated in Farooqabad, Sheikhupura Punjab. Guru Nanak as a young man was sent by his father Mehta Kalu to instill a sense of business in 
his son.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Dera Sahib
sikh-heritage.description: A Sikh temple in Lahore which commemorates the spot where the 5th guru of Sikhism was martyred in 1606. The gurdwara is located just outside of the Walled City of Lahore and is part of an ensemble of monuments.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib
sikh-heritage.description: Gurdwara Chowa Sahib is an abandoned gurdwara, located at the northern edge of the Rohtas Fort, near Jhelum, Punjab. The current building dates from 1834, and was commissioned by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

sikh-heritage.name: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur
sikh-heritage.description: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, also called Kartarpur Sahib, built on the historic site where the founder of Sikhism, Guru Nanak, settled and assembled the Sikh community. Notable for its location near the border between Pakistan and India.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Khunjerab
mountains-and-glaciers.description: A gateway between two great allies , the incredible altitude makes for a very memorable, albeit chilly, experience, which has captured the imaginations of the local people.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: K2
mountains-and-glaciers.description: The legendary K2 is the second highest mountain in the world. It is located in the north-western Karakoram Mountain Range on the PakistanâChina border

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Passu Cones
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Breathtaking views of majestic Passu Cones (few pointed cone-like snow covered peaks) are in the Karakorum Range in north of the Gulmit village in Gojal Valley.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Rakaposhi
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Part of the Karakoram range, Rakaposhi is the 27th highest mountain in the world. The mountain resides in the middle of the Bagrote valley, danyor and Nagar Valley.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Masherbrum
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Masherbrum, formerly known as K1 is located in the Ghanche District, Gilgit Baltistan. At 25,659 feet, it is the 22nd highest mountain in the world.  The mighty Masherbrum Peaks in Pakistan are perfect for every tough mountaineer to prepare themselves for higher altitude peaks.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Khunjerab National Park
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Khunjerab National Park is Pakistan's third largest national park. The park is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. The primary purpose of setting up this park was to provide protection to the endangered Marco polo sheep, which is only found in this area in Pakistan.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Karakoram Mountains
mountains-and-glaciers.description: The Karakoram is a mountain range spanning the borders of China, India, and Pakistan. The mountain range is a great challenge for the mountaineers & climbers the world over.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Diran peak
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Standing at the height of 7,266 Meters, Diran is a sight to behold. This pyramid shaped mountain is known as the most dangerous mountain of Pakistan due to large snow caps.

mountains-and-glaciers.name: Fairy Meadows
mountains-and-glaciers.description: Named by some German climbers and locally known as Jaugth, Fairy Meadows is a grassland near one of Nanga Parbat's base campsites.

beaches-and-islands.name: Mubarak Village Beach
beaches-and-islands.description: The crystal clear greenish-blue waters and unspoiled coastline have made this spot gain immense popularity in recent years. One can indulge in all sorts of water sports on the trip to Mubarak Village, including boating, beaching, snorkeling, and scuba diving.

beaches-and-islands.name: Kund Malir Beach
beaches-and-islands.description: Kund Malir beach with its sparkling cerulean waters, beckons visitors to spend the day picnicking or the night camping on its peaceful shore. Add a to that bonfire as the Milky Way unfolds above and it makes for the perfect weekend getaway.

beaches-and-islands.name: Jiwani Coastal Wetland
beaches-and-islands.description: Jiwani is a town and commercial port that is located along the Gulf of Oman in the Gawadar District of the Balochistan province in Pakistan.

beaches-and-islands.name: Sapat Beach
beaches-and-islands.description: Ranked as one of the best beaches in the world, Sapat beach, with its exceptional beauty is the best go-to place with family and friends.

beaches-and-islands.name: Bhit Khori
beaches-and-islands.description: Bhit Khori, one of the finest beaches in Pakistan, asks you to complete a rocky journey before it gifts you with its golden sands and beautiful, cerulean seawater.

beaches-and-islands.name: Manora Beach
beaches-and-islands.description: The long sandy beaches along the southern edge of the Manora Island are popular as Manora beach that is serving tourists as a popular picnic spot due to its incredible geographical location.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Attabad Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Attabad Lake is in Gojal region of Hunza -a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Kallar Kahar
valleys-and-lakes.description: Alluring scenic beauty, with a calm lake, and breathtaking views, where you can go for cliff-diving, paragliding and many more activities.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Soon Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Soon Valley is a breathtaking vista of natural beauty consisting of lakes and springs, lush green fertile fields. Accessible through Kallar Kahar, Soon Valley extends to almost 100 kilometers.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Neela Sandh Waterfall
valleys-and-lakes.description: Neela Sandh is a delightful waterfall, situated in Mori Syedan, Rawalpindi, Punjab. It has numerous greenery, tall trees and extensive mountains which are relatively secured with snow constantly. Guests who adore swimming unquestionably visit to enjoy with their families and companions.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Shandur Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Shandur Lake is located on a high mountain pass, âShandur Passâ. It is also called the âRoof of the Worldâ and is one of the most beautiful lakes of Pakistan. The spot is most well known in view of the Shandur Polo Festival.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Kai Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Kai Valley presents a picturesque panorama on both sides of the road. Kai Valley is one of the rare solitary landscapes which sees the majority of tourists. It gives the impression as if the hills were once underneath sea.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Shandur Pass
valleys-and-lakes.description: Known as the 'Roof of the World' where the Hindu Kush, Pamir Mountains and Karakorum Range meet, Shandur is located in the Upper Chitral District of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan and is location of annual Shandur Polo Festival.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Karimabad
valleys-and-lakes.description: Karimabad, previously known as Baltit, is named after Prince Karim Aga Khan IV. It is the capital of Hunza District, in the Gilgit-Baltistan area of Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Swaik Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Swaik Lake also known as âKhandowa Lakeâ is located in tehsil Kallar Kahar, Punjab. Itâs crystal clear water and serene atmosphere offers adventure lovers just the right mix of thrill with ease of access. It is a popular tourist attraction and offers opportunities for swimming and diving.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Khunjerab National Park
valleys-and-lakes.description: Khunjerab National Park is Pakistan's third largest national park. The park is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. The primary purpose of setting up this park was to provide protection to the endangered Marco polo sheep, which is only found in this area in Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Khaplu Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Khaplu is a city that serves as the managerial capital of the Ghanche District of Gilgit-Baltistan, in northern Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Karambar Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Karambar Lake, renowned as Qurumbar Lake, is a high height lake situated in the Ishkoman Valley bilanz in Ghizer District, Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Naltar Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: renowned for its lakes whose waters change colours depending on the time of day. The three lakes are known by several names. According to locals, one of the lakes is called the Pari Lake because of its enchanting, deep blue colour.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Phander Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Phander is the name of a settlement and valley in the Gupis-Yasin District of Pakistan's reliant region of Gilgit-Baltistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Hushe Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Hushe Valley is a valley in Ghanche District, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Created by the Hushe River, the valley runs from Masherbrum Mountain (at 7,821 meters) and close by glaciers south to the Shyok River, inverse Khaplu.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Baha Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Baha Lake is also known as Khukush Langar Lake is a colossal lake lying at the feet of transcending mountains.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Shogran Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Shogran, one of the most beautiful plateaus in Naran Valley.  From the rolling grassy lawns of the rest house, one can see breathtaking panoramic views of snow covered mountains.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Ishkoman
valleys-and-lakes.description: The Ishkoman valley lies in the north of Ghizer District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lining Afghanistan and the Pamir Wakhan Corridor.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Bagrote
valleys-and-lakes.description: Bagrote Valley is a valley in the Karakoram Mountain range in the GilgitâBaltistan district of northern Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Nagar
valleys-and-lakes.description: In an eponymous valley with splendid scenery, Nagar is a small town. A visit during the right season, you can see trees of many different colors with lakes, rivers, and clear skies abound.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Leepa Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Leepa Valley is located in Hattian Bala District of Azad Kashmir. With fields of rice apple found all over the valley, its lush green river fields in summer and typical wooden kashmiri houses present a wonderful view to the tourists.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Zharba Tso/Blind lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Zharba Tso or Blind lake is a Panoramic Lake close to Shigar around 170 km away from Skardu in Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Wali Tangi Dam Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Wali Tangi Dam is a little dam in the Urak Valley in Balochistan territory of Pakistan. It is arranged around 20 km east of Quetta at a rise of roughly 8,350 ft.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Neelum Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: The valley is situated in the northeast of Muzaffarabad, running parallel to Kaghan Valley. It is replete with gorgeous scenery, stunning valleys, and magical waterfalls.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Hunza Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Hunza is a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Keenjhar Lake Resort
valleys-and-lakes.description: The resort is developed on the bank of Keenjhar lake, which is a favorable and ideal place for winter migratory birds that come from regions of North Asia in the winter season. Located in the center of Thatta district, which has important tourist sites belonging to the near and far past of history.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Urak Valley
valleys-and-lakes.description: Urak Valley is a valley encircled by mountains inside the Quetta Area of Balochistan Region, in western Pakistan. Urak Valley is found close to Hana Lake and 28 kilometers (17 mi) from Quetta city.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Khalti Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Khalti Lake is located at Gupis-Yasin District, the westernmost piece of the GilgitâBaltistan locale and northernmost domain of Pakistan.

valleys-and-lakes.name: Rush Lake
valleys-and-lakes.description: Rush Lake is a high-altitude lake situated in Nagar Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan close to Rush Pari Peak. At 4,694 meters (15,400 ft), Rush is one of the most elevated high lakes on the planet.

sufi-tourism.name: Shrine of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
Tomb of Shah Shams Sabzwari Tabrez
Jamia Mosque Bhong
sufi-tourism.description: Bhong Mosque is located in the village of Bhong, Rahim Yar Khan District, Punjab Province. It was designed and constructed over a period of nearly 50 years.

sufi-tourism.name: Moti Mosque
sufi-tourism.description: Moti Masjid is a 17th-century religious building located inside the Lahore Fort, Lahore, and Punjab, Pakistan. It is a small, white marble structure built by Mughal emperor Jahangir.

sufi-tourism.name: Chaukhandi tombs
sufi-tourism.description: Chaukhandi Tombs, located about 29 km east of Karachi, Pakistan, are an ancient graveyard dating back to the 15thâ18th centuries. Known for their intricate sandstone carvings and pyramid-like structures, the tombs mostly belong to the Jokhio tribe and other local clans. Carvings on the graves reflect local art, culture, and traditionsâdepicting warriors, jewelry, and symbols of honor. Blending Islamic and Hindu design, these historic tombs offer a unique glimpse into Sindhâs rich heritage. Now protected and listed on UNESCOâs Tentative World Heritage List, the site is open to visitors seeking history and quiet reflection.

sufi-tourism.name: Shrine Khawaja Awais Kagha
sufi-tourism.description: Located in a cemetery in Dera Basti, Multan built around the year 1300 lies the tomb of Khawaja Awais Kagha who was a notable Sufi Wali. The tomb is decorated with blue and white glazed tiles covering the corner towers and portions of the facades.

sufi-tourism.name: Shahi Eid Gah Mosque
sufi-tourism.description: The mosque was funded by Nawab Abdul Samad Khan, who was the Mughal governor of Multan. The mosque is spacious, with a vast courtyard, a prayer chamber, and features seven domes and the mosque's exterior is embellished with glazed blue Multan-style tiles.

unesco-world-heritage-sites.name: Rohtas Fort
unesco-world-heritage-sites.description: Pashtun King Sher Shah Suri, the founder of short-lived Suri dynasty, built the Rohtas Fort in the 16th century. It is located near the city of Jhelum.

unesco-world-heritage-sites.name: Makli Necropolis
unesco-world-heritage-sites.description: Makli Necropolis near Thatta is one of the worldâs largest graveyards, home to stunning tombs and mausoleums from the 14th to 18th century. Its rich history and intricate art make it a remarkable heritage site.

unesco-world-heritage-sites.name: Mohenjo-daro
unesco-world-heritage-sites.description: Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BCE near Larkana, Sindh, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a marvel of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Its planned streets and smart drainage reflect a highly advanced urban life.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Rohtas Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Pashtun King Sher Shah Suri, the founder of short-lived Suri dynasty, built the Rohtas Fort in the 16th century. It is located near the city of Jhelum.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Tomb of Jahangir
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The mausoleum dates from 1637, and is located in Shahdara Bagh in Lahore. The site is famous for its interiors that are extensively embellished with frescoes and marble. The tomb is a part of an ensemble currently on the tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage status.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Bhodesar Mosque
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: This mosque with white pillars in Bhodesar is a small marble and limestone structure near the pond embankment is built in 1436 AD. It was built by Mehmood Shah Bin Zaffar Shah, ruler of Gujrat. The mosque is located 5 Km from town Nagarparkar.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Harappa
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Harappa
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Harappa is a large village, presently in the province of Punjab. The modern town is a part of and lies next to the ancient city. The site of the ancient city contains the ruins of a Bronze Age fortified city.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Kargah Buddha
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: About 9.7km away from Gilgit, this carved image is part of an archaeological site which stands 50 feet high.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Gumti Water Fountain
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Gumti Water Fountain is a monument in Faisalabad, Pakistan preserved from the British Raj era. It was a general meeting place of the city folk for local town meetings.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Attock Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Attock Fort was constructed in 1581 on the orders of the Mughal Emperor Akbar to protect the passage of the River Indus. It is located at a distance of 80 km from the capital city of Islamabad.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Multan Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: A military installation built between 800 and 1000 B.C. The fort originally known as Katochgarh and is attributed to have been built by the Katoch Dynasty was notable for both its effectiveness as a defense installation and for its architecture.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Haveli Barood Khana
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Built in the 18th century by a Sikh commanding general and used as a house. Considering the hot temperature of Lahore, the haveli has high ceilings. The room also has murals of the Sikh general fighting demons.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Altit fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: An ancient fort at Altit town in the Hunza valley in Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan, it was originally home to the hereditary rulers of the Hunza state.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Naukot Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The fort was used by Talpur Mirs as a strong hold cum-residence. Most probably these buildings were used as residences and a few of them for imprisoning the prisoners.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Seri Bahlol
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Seri Bahlol, likewise Sahr-I Bahlol or Sahri Bahlol, is a city and archeological site situated close to Takht-I-Bahi, in Mardan District, around 70-kilometer north-west of Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The haveli is considered to be one of the finest examples of Sikh architecture in Lahore preserved in its original architecture.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Khaplu Palace
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Khaplu Palace is also known as Yabgo Khar (meaning "The fort of Doqsa"), is an old fort located in Khaplu, within the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Qutb-ud-Din Aibak's Tomb
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture. Prior to the modern construction, the Sultan's grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Pharwala Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Pharwala Fort is a 15th-century fort built by the Gakhars located in Rawalpindi. The fort is naturally defended on one side by a small Himalayan range and the other by the Soan River.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Kharpocho Skardu Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The Skardu fort also known as called kharapocho is a stunning and historically significant fort of the Baltistan area.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Sadhu da Bagh caves
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The village is believed to be more than seven hundred years old. Relics of the Buddhist era, dating back to the 8th century can be found here. Archaeological evidence indicates that the caves and the platform-like formations surrounding the area were first used for meditation.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Makli Necropolis
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Makli Necropolis near Thatta is one of the worldâs largest graveyards, home to stunning tombs and mausoleums from the 14th to 18th century. Its rich history and intricate art make it a remarkable heritage site.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Sethi street
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Made in the nineteenth century Finely assembled 05 places of Sethi family are situated here close by other houses.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Mohenjo-daro
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Mohenjo-daro, built around 2500 BCE near Larkana, Sindh, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a marvel of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. Its planned streets and smart drainage reflect a highly advanced urban life.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Amburiq Mosque
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Located in Shigar, The Amburiq Mosque is one of the oldest mosques in the region.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Giri Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Giri Fort built in the fifth century perhaps as a stronghold for the thousands of monks in Taxila Valley. Two groups of Buddhist establishments are found here, a fort, a Muslim Ziarat and mosques, all ranging from the early Kushana period to the time of Akbar.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Old Jamia Masjid Thatta
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The large brick masonry structure, built by Samma ruler Jam Tamachi, as homage to the Sufi saint. The masonry walls are in a highly degraded state with a collapsed roof showing its age.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Shigar Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The Shigar Fort means that The Fort on Rock. It is an old building of Baltistan set within the city of Shigar.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Meeran Ja Qubba
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The tombs of Talpur Mirs have been built since the British conquest. From an architectural point of view they are conspicuously inferior to those of Kalhoras. For some time these tombs were maintained by their families.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Lansdowne Bridge
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The Lansdowne Bridge is a 19th-century bridge that spans the Indus River between the cities of Sukkur and Rohri, in Sindh.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Noor Mahal
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: Bahawalpur, due to the lack of publicity.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Faiz Mahal
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: A grand architectural masterpiece, unique traditional culture and traditional work of art seems to have swept over the real splendor. Details on the walls of the palace are exquisitely designed, exhibiting the fine art of the people of past era.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Mohatta Palace Museum
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The Mohatta Palace Museum offers a diverse range of activities for both the casual and informed visitor. Families and school children are particularly welcome and tours can be arranged in advance.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Kotdiji Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: This magnificent fort made from kiln baked bricks sits atop a high semi-circular lime stone hillock. Fifty strategically erected bastions for cannons and to keep a vigilant eye over enemy movement. Its beautifully carved arches & the platform attract the visitors eye immediately.

heritage-and-archaeology-sites.name: Umerkot Fort
heritage-and-archaeology-sites.description: The walls both on its interior & exterior give a tapered look, well supported on all the four corners with semi-circular bastions. On the east side there is an arched gateway flanked by semi-circular bastions.

hindu-and-jain-temples.name: Jain Temple
hindu-and-jain-temples.description: The temple is made of stone and consists of an open group of pillars with carved capitals. From this temple was found a beautifully carved block of marble which is now on display in the National Museum of Pakistan, Karachi.

hindu-and-jain-temples.name: Sadh Belo
hindu-and-jain-temples.description: An island on Indus River very close to the city of Sukkur, There is a Hindu temple on the island which was founded in 1823 by Swami Bakhandi Maharaj Udasi. Provides the tourist with a pleasurable experience and scenic view of River Indus.

hindu-and-jain-temples.name: Malot Temples
hindu-and-jain-temples.description: Malot Hindu Temples are located in the Salt Range of Pakistan near the city of Kallar Kahar. A serene place where the cliffs by the temple present a beautiful panoramic view.

hindu-and-jain-temples.name: Gori Temple
hindu-and-jain-temples.description: Despite the effects of fire and gun powder, it is the best surviving temple here, built of local stone with pillars and details of marble from Rajputana.  The shrine itself which formerly had a âSikharaâ of typical Kathiawar type is now adorned with rows of miniature âSikharasâ.
